Pick-me
PIK-mee
noun / adjective (Gen-Z slang)
From the plea "pick me!" — a child begging to be chosen. Black Twitter popularized "pick-me" around 2016–2017 ("pick me, choose me, love me," echoing a line from the TV drama Grey’s Anatomy), and TikTok spread "pick-me girl" in 2020–2021 for a young woman who wins male approval by distancing herself from and disparaging other women ("I’m not like other girls"). A "pick-me boy" variant exists.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a pick-me is someone, usually a girl, who seeks the approval of the opposite sex by putting down her own: "I’m not like other girls, I don’t wear makeup, I just hang out with the guys." The word is an insult, and a sharp one. The Christian observation: the slang has spotted a real sin and then wields it carelessly. The sin is the old one of John 12: "they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God" (Joh 12:43). The pick-me buys favour by self-advertising and by belittling others, and Scripture forbids both: "Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth" (Pro 27:2), and "in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves" (Php 2:3). Paul refused the bargain entirely: "if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ" (Gal 1:10). But the insult is often aimed at girls who are simply different — quieter, plainer, less interested in trends — and that is cruelty, not discernment. Titus 2 offers the better path: older women teaching younger women (Tit 2:3–4), girls bound together rather than competing for boys’ attention. A father tells his daughter: you do not need to be picked; you have been chosen — and the girls around you are sisters to honour, not rivals to undercut.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (Black Twitter c. 2016; TikTok 2020) for one who seeks the opposite sex’s approval by disparaging her own — loving the praise of men; Scripture answers with chosenness in Christ and esteeming others better.

PICK-ME, n. / adj. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2016–present) One who seeks the approval of the opposite sex by disparaging others of her own sex. "‘I’m not like other girls’ is such a pick-me line."

Pick-me girl, pick-me boy; pick-me behaviour.

From the plea "pick me, choose me, love me."

Webster (1828), root word pick: “PICK, verb transitive [&hellip;] 1. To pull off or pluck with the fingers something that grows or adheres to another thing; to separate by the hand, as fruit from trees; as, to pick apples or oranges; to pick strawberries. 2. To pull off or separate with the teeth, beak or claws; as, to pick flesh from a bone; hence, 3.”

Decode for parents: a real vice and a ready insult. Teach your daughter she is chosen, and not to throw the word at the quiet girl.

Key Scripture

Joh 12:43 — "For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God."

Pro 27:2 — "Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips."

Php 2:3 — "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves."

Gal 1:10 — "For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ."

Tit 2:4 — "That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,"

Modern Corruption

Pick-me names the love of men’s praise bought by belittling other women, then becomes a weapon against any girl who is different; Scripture rebukes both the vice and the cruelty.

expand to see more

The pick-me posture is a small economy of approval: I lower my sisters so that I will look better to the boys. Scripture calls it what it is — loving "the praise of men more than the praise of God" (Joh 12:43) — and gives two commands that undo it: let others praise you (Pro 27:2), and esteem others better than yourself (Php 2:3).

But the slang is also used cruelly. The quiet girl, the girl who prefers fishing to fashion, the girl who will not join the gossip, all get called pick-mes. That is the mean-girl version of the same sin. Paul’s alternative is a community of women teaching and loving one another (Tit 2:3–4). Tell your daughter she does not need to be picked; in Christ she is chosen.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Child’s plea "pick me!" → "pick me, choose me, love me" (TV drama line) → c. 2016 Black Twitter "pick-me" → 2020–2021 TikTok "pick-me girl."
